messages:
Ivy Nguyen: Hey team, first morning—my Lenovo X13 arrived and boots Ubuntu 22.04. When I tried to enroll via the Fleet SSO flow it failed with 'device not associated with org' and then after a reboot the machine dropped to emergency mode complaining about LUKS and mounting root. I'm blocked and can't get to the desktop. Who should I bug for a reimage or a recovery key?

Blake (IT): Welcome Ivy! :wave: Sorry for the rough start. Can you DM me a photo of the screen and the serial (bottom sticker or `sudo dmidecode -s system-serial-number`)? Do you recall if you accepted any disk encryption during OOBE?

Ivy Nguyen: DM'd the photo. Serial from dmidecode: R9C12345. During OOBE I chose the default (encrypt disk) and signed in with SSO but the Fleet enroll step errored before finishing. The emergency prompt shows: "cryptsetup: LUKS header OK, no key available for keyslot 1".

Rowan - Endpoint Admin: Thanks. Sounds like the device was encrypted at staging and the TPM binding step didn't finish so there's no escrowed LUKS passphrase in our key management. We're seeing similar for a small batch that missed the final provision hook. Fleet-bot, check device R9C12345 in staging inventory.

fleet-bot: Fleet lookup: device(serial=R9C12345) -> recorded by staging-02 on 2026-09-12T16:04:07Z. Enrollment state: incomplete. LUKS escrow: MISSING.

Blake (IT): Ok that matches. Two safe choices: 1) Reimage (fast, destroys local data) which will produce a clean device and enroll correctly, or 2) If you have critical data (you said no) we can attempt to pull the key from staging lab (low chance) and try recovery. Which do you want?

Ivy Nguyen: No data—reimage is fine. I mostly need dev tools (Pyenv, Docker, VSCode WSL-equivalent) to be ready. Could you reimage and tag it for Linux dev?

Rowan - Endpoint Admin: Reimage queued. We'll push the company's Linux provisioning image (includes Fleet agent, MDM hooks, and automatic LUKS escrow to our Key Vault). Keep it on AC power and connected to wired or hotspot during reprovision.

fleet-bot: Reimage job 'linux-provision-1792001111' started by Rowan at 2026-09-14T08:12:30Z. Estimated 12-20 minutes.

Ivy Nguyen: Device went through installer and I see Fleet SSO prompt now. I completed SSO and landed on the desktop. Company Fleet app shows "Pending policies: linux-dev".

Rowan - Endpoint Admin: Great. Run `sudo journalctl -u fleet -n 200 --no-pager | tail -n 10` and paste if you see any errors. Also run `sudo cryptsetup luksDump /dev/nvme0n1p3 | grep -i "Key Slot"` to confirm passphrase binding.

Ivy Nguyen: `sudo journalctl -u fleet -n 200 --no-pager | tail -n 10` -> no errors, last lines: "agent: enrolled: success, policy apply: linux-dev -> success". `sudo cryptsetup luksDump /dev/nvme0n1p3 | grep -i "Key Slot"` -> shows Key Slot 0: ENABLED.

Rowan - Endpoint Admin: Perfect. LUKS keyslot present and our escrow agent pushed the protector to the Key Vault. I'm going to create a temporary sudo elevation for you (add to sudoers group) for 3 hours so you can install Docker and system dev packages. We avoid making everyone a permanent admin.

Blake (IT): Granting temp sudo via ephemeral group 'temp-sudo-3h' now. You should be able to run `sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y build-essential docker.io python3-venv` and `snap install --classic code`.

fleet-bot: Action 'temp-sudo-3h' assigned to IVY\ivy.nguyen by Blake at 2026-09-14T08:42:00Z. Expires at 2026-09-14T11:42:00Z.

Ivy Nguyen: Installing now. Quick question: do we prefer `docker.io` or `docker-ce` from Docker repos?

Blake (IT): We standardize on the distro package (`docker.io`) for stability unless you need the newest features. If you do, ping and we'll approve adding the Docker APT repo.

Ivy Nguyen: All installs completed, docker runs (`sudo docker run hello-world` worked), pyenv set up, VSCode snap installed. Fleet shows device compliant and LUKS escrow verified. Thanks everyone!

Rowan - Endpoint Admin: Nice work. We'll let the temp sudo expire automatically. Welcome to Redwood, Ivy! If anything odd pops up ping this thread or DM me.

Ivy Nguyen: Thanks y'all, appreciate the help :tada:
